body:
You are drafting dialogue for "Curse of Strahd", a single-player D&D 5e (2024 rules) computer game set in Barovia. I need about 30 lines for ONE group of scenes in this message (a second message will ask for the next group). Reply with plain text only: the lines under the node names given below, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The situation

Ireena Kolyana is a tall red-haired woman in her early twenties, the adopted daughter of the late burgomaster of the village of Barovia. The vampire lord Strahd hunts her. The player's party has left her to shelter in the town of Vallaki, either at the Blue Water Inn or in St. Andral's church, and has gone about its business.

Izek Strazni is the Baron's enforcer in Vallaki: a big scarred man in a watch captain's coat whose right arm is not his own (scaled red-black to the shoulder, clawed, hot, and able to burst into flame). When he was nine, wolves took his little sister in the woods by the lake, and took his arm too. He has dreamed of a red-haired woman every night since and pays the toymaker to carve dolls of her face. He has seen Ireena. Neither of them knows she is his lost sister, and he does not know it either; he only knows he wants her, safe, near him, never in the woods again.

A visit now comes to the party, at night, while the party is somewhere in Vallaki (the inn, the church, or the town square): somebody local brings them news about Izek and Ireena. There are three stages, each its own scene, played at different nights:

1. OMEN. Izek has taken to standing, motionless, outside the place where Ireena sleeps, staring at her window. Nothing has happened yet. A warning.
2. TAKEN. Some nights later, during the small hours, Izek walked in (the inn) or through the churchyard (the church) and carried her off to his room in the Baron's mansion. He did not hurt her; she is unhurt as far as anyone knows. Nobody stopped him. She is in his room, off the great hall. The door is not locked. He sits in front of it.
3. ESCAPE. Two days later, nobody having come for her, she got out by herself: she hit Izek in the face with a brass candlestick in front of six of the Baron's watch, broke his nose, and walked out of the mansion's front door past men who did not know whether to stop her. The watch saw it; he is humiliated. She is back at her refuge, bruised and colder toward the party, who did not come.

Who brings the news depends on where the party is when the visit finds them: at the Blue Water Inn it is URWIN (the innkeeper); at St. Andral's it is FATHER LUCIAN; anywhere else in Vallaki it is a TOWN GUARD (a watchman of the Baron). Whatever the speaker says must read correctly whichever refuge Ireena was in (the inn or the church), so speaker lines are written NEUTRAL about which refuge ("where she sleeps", "her room", "the door") - the Narrator lines, which come first, say which refuge it is.

What the player sees, in order: a Narrator line for the refuge (two versions: inn / church), then the speaker for where the party stands (three versions), then a small menu of what the party can say. Every scene ends the conversation.

## The nodes I need (one line = 1-2 short sentences)

omen_inn: Narrator x1 (a big man stands motionless in the dark street across from the inn, looking up at one shuttered window; the faint red glow of his arm; he has plainly been there for hours)
omen_church: Narrator x1 (the same man at the churchyard gate, one hand on the iron, not coming in; nothing supernatural, just him standing there in the dark looking at the vestry window)
omen_urwin: Urwin x2 (what he has seen: the man has stood there since dusk; nobody dares move him; a warning in his few dry words)
omen_lucian: Father Lucian x2 (the same, in his kind tired voice; a priest who would take her in and knows holy ground does not stop a living man)
omen_guard: Town Guard x2 (the same, in the nervous bureaucratic cheer of the watch: the captain is not ours to order; please do not tell the Baron I said so)
omen_menu: option texts only, one `* ` line: what the party says as the way out (e.g. that they will watch him themselves). Under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we").

taken_inn: Narrator x1 (the party sees Ireena's room at the inn: bed empty, a candle burned down on the floor, the door off one hinge; what a quiet taking leaves behind)
taken_church: Narrator x1 (the vestry bed where she slept: empty, blanket on the floor, the churchyard gate standing open)
taken_urwin: Urwin x3 (he saw Izek take her at the third watch, quietly, as one carries a sleeping child; she did not scream; he did not stop him and is ashamed; he says where: the Baron's mansion, Izek's room off the great hall, the door not locked, Izek sits in front of it)
taken_lucian: Father Lucian x3 (he was at vespers when it happened; the door was not barred; a living man needs no invitation; he blames himself; where she is, the same facts)
taken_guard: Town Guard x3 (Captain Izek carried the red-haired lady to the mansion; nobody asked; orders, he says; where she is, the same facts; please do not tell the Baron)
taken_ismark: Narrator x1 (used only when Ismark (Ireena's adoptive brother, the burgomaster's son, who stayed behind to guard her) was guarding her: he went after them to the mansion gate and the watch turned him back at spear-point; he is out there now, shouting; the party finds him gone from his post)
taken_menu: option texts only, one `* ` line: the party says they are going after her. Under 12 words.

escape_inn: Narrator x1 (the inn's upper room is lit again; a basin of pink water; Ireena sits on the bed with her knuckles bound and does not look up)
escape_church: Narrator x1 (the vestry: Ireena sits very upright on the bed with her hand wrapped in a cloth, a candle burning, and does not look up)
escape_urwin: Urwin x2 (what the whole town now knows: she broke his nose with a candlestick in front of the watch and walked out of the front door; he saw her come back at first light; she asked for nothing)
escape_lucian: Father Lucian x2 (the same, in his voice; he is quietly proud and quietly shaken; she did not come to the church for blessing but for a basin; she asked if the party had come)
escape_guard: Town Guard x2 (the same: six of us stood there and not one moved; the Captain has not been seen since, and nobody is laughing aloud; please do not tell the Baron I said any of this)
escape_menu: option texts only, one `* ` line: the party says they will go and see her. Under 12 words.

That is 29 spoken lines and 4 option texts.

## Canon limits

Do not invent names, places or history beyond what is given: no new named characters (the Baron is only "the Baron"; the innkeepers are Urwin and his wife, who need not appear); no new places beyond the inn, the church, the churchyard gate, the square, the Baron's mansion with Izek's room off the great hall; no new monsters. The Baron's mansion is real and the Baron's men are "the watch". Izek is "the Captain" to the watch and "Izek" to everyone else. He does NOT hurt Ireena; nobody says he did. He took her because he wants to keep her; the speakers do not know why and may guess ("the dolls", "he's been odd about her"). Nobody in these scenes knows she is his sister. Nobody says Strahd's name. In the church scenes, the bones of St. Andral may or may not be back: do not mention the bones. Ireena is not in these scenes (she is only reported). The cost of the party's absence falls on Ireena's trust and Izek's pride, not on anything the speakers say they lost. Moods: a speaker may use [afraid], [sad], [weary], [smile] or [angry], or no mood; the Narrator never has a mood.

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Speaker [mood]: Text` where Speaker is Narrator, Urwin, Father Lucian or Town Guard. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 22 words in total, written to be spoken aloud: NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. Plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names above, each node on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. For the option texts write one `* text` row under that node. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.

## Voice bibles and existing lines (match the register; do not repeat these)

URWIN (speaker `Urwin`). Quiet innkeeper with black hair and black eyes; listens to the room more than he serves it. Secretly one of the Keepers of the Feather, who watch the valley as ravens (do NOT mention this). Few words, all useful. Statements, not questions. Dry, never cruel.
- "Bed's upstairs, meal's on the stove. Questions are free. I might not answer them."
- "Back. Good."
- "Nothing comes in through our windows that we don't let in."
- "Lucian's stripped his altar. Something's gone from the church that shouldn't have."
- "We'll still give you a bed. Danika says it's what you do. We won't sell you anything. I say that's what you do."

FATHER LUCIAN (speaker `Father Lucian`). Careful, kind, tired priest, twenty years at St. Andral's. Plain, warm, a little formal; asks before he tells; keeps catching his sermon instincts and trimming them. Fears he is a coward for not choosing a side. Hope is "the only tool they let me keep".
- "Are you hurt, or hungry, or in trouble? Those are the three reasons people come here now."
- "You held. All night, you held. I've lit a candle for each of you, and one for the windows, which did not."
- "Vargas is a frightened child with a whip. Fiona is a patient woman with a much worse master."
- "Go with God, and come back to us."
- "Gently."

TOWN GUARD (speaker `Town Guard`). Ordinary men with festival ribbons on their spears and orders to report frowning. Bureaucratic cheer over exhaustion. They say the quiet part and then ask you not to repeat it.
- "Halt. Names, business, and how long you mean to stay. And smile, please. It's the law this week."
- "Last week was the Festival of the Returning Swallows. No swallows came. It was still a great success."
- "Same lockup, same key, different people. I'm still here. Somebody has to hold the key."
- "Kolyan's girl? From the village? We heard he'd died. Sorry, miss. The Baron will want to know you're here."

IZEK (he is not in these scenes, but the speakers are describing him). Flat, short, imperatives and threats; never more than two sentences unless he speaks of her. About her he goes quiet and almost gentle, which is worse. Pet phrases: "Not here." "I'm good at waiting."
- "I've seen you. Every night since I was nine years old. I didn't know your name. Now I do."
- "Something took my arm when I was nine and gave me this one. Nothing's frightened me since."

IREENA (she is only reported here, but her trust is the cost). Proud, direct, dry; judges the party by how they treat her father; refuses to be a damsel.
- "I slept through the night. The whole night. I'd forgotten that was a thing people did."
- "Izek comes to the church door at dusk. He doesn't come in. He can't, or he won't. He just stands there."
- "The Martikovs are kind. Urwin sits up all night watching the windows. I've never met a man so interested in birds."

## The Narrator

An old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather. Second person or plain scene description, present tense. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn (irony, dread, dry joke). Ominous, dryly funny, never cruel. Concrete senses over adjectives (a smell, a sound, a temperature). No game terms: never "roll", "check", "DC", "HP", "level". No winks at the player. Here the Narrator is quiet and exact: this is dread, then shame, then a small grim satisfaction.
Samples:
- "The hall smells of beeswax and old smoke. Somebody kept this house beautifully, right up until they didn't."
- "A big man in a watch captain's coat stops dead in the middle of the square. His right arm is wrong: scaled red-black to the shoulder, with claws where the nails should be."
- "He doesn't move until Ireena turns away. Then he watches her go, and goes on watching the place where she was."
- "The Baron's fist went quiet as a struck bell."

~ omen_inn
Narrator: A big man stands motionless in the dark street across from the inn, staring up at one shuttered window. The red-black scales of his arm give the mud at his boots a faint, patient glow.

~ omen_church
Narrator: A big man stands at the churchyard gate with one clawed hand on the iron, looking at the vestry window. Nothing stops him from coming in, which makes his waiting worse.

~ omen_urwin
Urwin: Izek has been out there since dusk, watching the window where she sleeps.
Urwin [weary]: Nobody on the street goes near him. If you mean to keep her, don't leave her long.

~ omen_lucian
Father Lucian [weary]: Forgive me, friends, Izek has stood outside since dusk, watching the room where she sleeps.
Father Lucian [sad]: A threshold only keeps out the dead. It will not stop a living man when he decides to walk through.

~ omen_guard
Town Guard [smile]: Evening, friends, and keep smiling. The Captain has stood outside her window since dusk, though I'm sure it's strictly official.
Town Guard [afraid]: He isn't ours to question when he gets that look. Please don't tell the Baron I mentioned it.

~ omen_menu
* We'll keep watch on him ourselves.

~ taken_inn
Narrator: The bed in the upper room is empty, a tallow candle burned down to grease on the floorboards. The door hangs off one hinge, which is all the noise a large man needed to make.

~ taken_church
Narrator: The narrow cot in the vestry is empty, its wool blanket dragged across the stone floor. Outside, the iron gate stands wide to the dark street.

~ taken_urwin
Urwin [weary]: Third watch. Izek walked in, lifted her out of bed like a sleeping child, and carried her out.
Urwin [sad]: She didn't scream, and I didn't draw on him. Say what you like about that.
Urwin: He took her to the Baron's mansion, to his room off the great hall. The door's unlocked, and he's sitting in front of it.

~ taken_lucian
Father Lucian [sad]: I was at prayers when he came, and the door was not barred. A living man needs no invitation.
Father Lucian [weary]: He carried her out in her cloak without an unkind word, and I had only an old man's hands to raise.
Father Lucian: She is in the Baron's mansion, in Izek's room off the great hall. The door is unlocked, and he sits before it.

~ taken_guard
Town Guard [afraid]: Captain Izek carried the red-haired lady up to the Baron's mansion before dawn. Orders, he said, and nobody asked whose.
Town Guard: He didn't lay a rough hand on her, mind. Just took her up to his room off the great hall.
Town Guard [afraid]: The door isn't even locked, he just sits in the chair outside it. Please don't tell the Baron I told you.

~ taken_ismark
Narrator: Her brother's post by the door is empty. He followed them as far as the mansion gates, where he is currently shouting himself hoarse against four watchmen's spears.

~ taken_menu
* We're going to the mansion for her now.

~ escape_inn
Narrator: The upper room is lit again, a tin basin of pink water cooling on the washstand. Ireena sits on the edge of the bed with her knuckles bound in linen and does not look up.

~ escape_church
Narrator: A single candle burns in the vestry, where Ireena sits very straight on the narrow cot. Her right hand is wrapped in clean linen, and she does not look toward the door.

~ escape_urwin
Urwin: She came back at first light and asked for water and clean linen. Nothing else.
Urwin [smile]: Word is she broke Izek's nose with a brass candlestick in front of six watchmen and walked out the front door.

~ escape_lucian
Father Lucian [weary]: She returned at dawn, asking not for a blessing, only for a basin of cold water. She asked if you had come.
Father Lucian: They say she struck Izek across the face with a heavy candlestick and walked straight past six of the watch.

~ escape_guard
Town Guard [afraid]: The red-haired lady broke the Captain's nose with a brass candlestick and walked right out the front doors. Six of us stood there, and not one man moved.
Town Guard [weary]: The Captain hasn't come out of his room since, and nobody is laughing where he can hear. Don't tell the Baron I said so.

~ escape_menu
* We'll go in and speak with her.
